_meta.description: Chess Theory Database - Opening and Endgame patterns with explanations
_meta.instructions: Add patterns here. The system will match positions and provide explanations.

opening_theory._description: Opening patterns: position + mistake + correct move + explanation

italian_two_knights_d5.name: Two Knights Defense - Premature d5
italian_two_knights_d5.explanation: In the Two Knights Defense, d5 is premature when White hasn't played Ng5. After exd5, Black loses central control and faces tactical problems.
italian_two_knights_d5.why_bad: After exd5 Nxd5, Black's center crumbles. The e5 pawn becomes weak.
italian_two_knights_d5.why_good: d6 supports the e5 pawn, keeps the center solid, and prepares Be7 + O-O.
italian_two_knights_d5.rule: In the Italian/Two Knights, d5 is only good AFTER Ng5. Play d6 first.

italian_giuoco_piano_d5.name: Giuoco Piano - Premature d5
italian_giuoco_piano_d5.explanation: In the Giuoco Piano, d5 gives up the center. d6 is the main line - solid and flexible.
italian_giuoco_piano_d5.why_bad: d5 opens the position when you're not fully developed. White gets active play.
italian_giuoco_piano_d5.why_good: d6 maintains tension, supports e5, and allows flexible development.
italian_giuoco_piano_d5.rule: In the Italian Game, keep the center solid with d6 unless you have a specific tactical reason for d5.

sicilian_premature_d5.name: Sicilian Defense - Premature d5
sicilian_premature_d5.explanation: In the Sicilian, Black should play d6 first to support the c5 pawn. d5 is premature.
sicilian_premature_d5.why_bad: After exd5, Black has no central pawns and White controls the center.
sicilian_premature_d5.why_good: d6 prepares a solid structure. d5 comes later after proper preparation.
sicilian_premature_d5.rule: In the Sicilian, play d6 first. Prepare d5 with pieces, not rush it.

french_attack_chain.name: French Defense - Pawn Chain Attack
french_attack_chain.explanation: In the French, attack the BASE of the pawn chain (d4) with c5, not the HEAD (e5) with f6.
french_attack_chain.why_bad: f6 attacks the strong part of the chain. After exf6, Black's kingside is weakened.
french_attack_chain.why_good: c5 attacks d4, the base. If White doesn't defend properly, the whole chain collapses.
french_attack_chain.rule: In the French, attack the pawn chain base with c5, not the head with f6.

caro_kann_solid_d5.name: Caro-Kann Defense - Support d5
caro_kann_solid_d5.explanation: In the main line Caro-Kann, capture dxe4 to challenge White's center. e6 is passive.
caro_kann_solid_d5.why_bad: e6 blocks the light-squared bishop and gives White a space advantage.
caro_kann_solid_d5.why_good: dxe4 forces White to recapture, then Bf5 develops with tempo.
caro_kann_solid_d5.rule: In the Caro-Kann, capture dxe4 and develop Bf5 - that's the whole point of the opening.

queens_gambit_hold_d5.name: Queen's Gambit - Don't Grab c4
queens_gambit_hold_d5.explanation: In the Queen's Gambit, accepting with dxc4 gives up the center. e6 maintains central control.
queens_gambit_hold_d5.why_bad: After dxc4, White plays e4 and dominates the center. The c4 pawn is hard to hold.
queens_gambit_hold_d5.why_good: e6 supports d5, prepares Nf6 and Bd6. Black keeps equal chances.
queens_gambit_hold_d5.rule: In the Queen's Gambit, don't grab the pawn unless you know the theory. e6 or c6 are safe.

london_system_challenge.name: London System - Challenge the Bishop
london_system_challenge.explanation: Against the London, challenge the center with c5 instead of pinning with Bg4.
london_system_challenge.why_bad: Bg4 doesn't challenge White's setup. White plays e3 and has a comfortable position.
london_system_challenge.why_good: c5 attacks d4 immediately and challenges White's central control.
london_system_challenge.rule: Against the London, play c5 early to challenge the center. Don't just develop passively.

endgame_theory._description: Endgame patterns with rules to remember

king_and_pawn_opposition.name: King and Pawn - Opposition
king_and_pawn_opposition.key_rule: The attacking king must get in FRONT of the pawn to win.
king_and_pawn_opposition.explanation: With king and pawn vs king, the attacker wins only if their king reaches the 6th rank in front of the pawn.
king_and_pawn_opposition.common_mistake: Pushing the pawn before the king is in front
king_and_pawn_opposition.correct_technique: Use the king to gain opposition, then advance the pawn
king_and_pawn_opposition.rule: King in FRONT of the pawn wins. King BEHIND the pawn draws.

rook_endgame_activity.name: Rook Endgames - Rook Activity
rook_endgame_activity.key_rule: Rook activity is more important than material.
rook_endgame_activity.explanation: In rook endgames, an active rook on the 7th rank is often worth more than a pawn.
rook_endgame_activity.correct_technique: Activate your rook even if it costs a pawn
rook_endgame_activity.rule: Active rook > extra pawn. Get your rook to the 7th rank.

rook_behind_passed_pawn.name: Rook Endgames - Rook Behind Passed Pawn
rook_behind_passed_pawn.key_rule: Place your rook BEHIND passed pawns (yours or opponent's).
rook_behind_passed_pawn.explanation: A rook behind a passed pawn gains activity as the pawn advances. A rook in front loses activity.
rook_behind_passed_pawn.common_mistake: Putting rook in front of passed pawn
rook_behind_passed_pawn.correct_technique: Rook behind your passed pawn to support. Rook behind opponent's to stop it.
rook_behind_passed_pawn.rule: Rooks belong BEHIND passed pawns, never in front.

lucena_position.name: Lucena Position - Building a Bridge
lucena_position.key_rule: Win by building a bridge with your rook.
lucena_position.explanation: With rook and pawn on the 7th rank and enemy king cut off, use your rook to block checks - the bridge technique.
lucena_position.common_mistake: Trying to promote immediately without the bridge
lucena_position.correct_technique: Rook to the 4th rank, then use it to shield the king from checks
lucena_position.rule: Lucena: Build the bridge. Rook to 4th rank, then shield the king.

philidor_position.name: Philidor Position - Third Rank Defense
philidor_position.key_rule: Defend by keeping your rook on the 3rd rank until the pawn advances.
philidor_position.explanation: With rook and pawn vs rook, the defender draws by keeping their rook on the 3rd rank, then going to the back rank when the pawn advances.
philidor_position.common_mistake: Going to the back rank too early
philidor_position.correct_technique: Stay on 3rd rank. Only go to back rank when pawn reaches 6th.
philidor_position.rule: Philidor defense: 3rd rank until pawn advances, then back rank for checks.

opposite_bishops_draw.name: Opposite Colored Bishops - Drawing Tendency
opposite_bishops_draw.key_rule: Opposite colored bishops favor the defender.
opposite_bishops_draw.explanation: With opposite colored bishops, even a 2-pawn advantage may not be enough to win.
opposite_bishops_draw.correct_technique: Place pawns on squares your bishop controls, blockade on enemy bishop color
opposite_bishops_draw.rule: Opposite bishops: defense has huge drawing chances. Don't trade into this if you're winning!

knight_vs_bishop_endgame.name: Knight vs Bishop - Pawn Structure
knight_vs_bishop_endgame.key_rule: Knight prefers closed positions, bishop prefers open positions.
knight_vs_bishop_endgame.explanation: Knights are better with locked pawns. Bishops are better in open positions with pawns on both sides.
knight_vs_bishop_endgame.common_mistake: Not considering pawn structure when trading pieces
knight_vs_bishop_endgame.correct_technique: Trade into knight endgame if position is closed. Trade into bishop endgame if open.
knight_vs_bishop_endgame.rule: Knight = closed positions. Bishop = open positions with pawns on both sides.

tactical_patterns._description: Common tactical patterns and their rules

undefended_piece.name: Undefended Pieces
undefended_piece.rule: Before EVERY move, check: Are any of my pieces undefended?
undefended_piece.explanation: Many tactics work because a piece was left undefended.

pin_to_king.name: Pin to the King
pin_to_king.trigger: Piece on line between attacker and king
pin_to_king.rule: Avoid placing valuable pieces on lines with your king.
pin_to_king.explanation: A pinned piece cannot move without exposing the king to check.

knight_fork.name: Knight Fork
knight_fork.rule: Watch for knight fork squares when your king and queen are on the same color complex.
knight_fork.explanation: Knights can attack multiple pieces at once. The most deadly forks target king and queen.

back_rank_weakness.name: Back Rank Mate
back_rank_weakness.trigger: King trapped on back rank with no escape squares
back_rank_weakness.rule: Give your king an escape square (luft) - push h6 or g6.
back_rank_weakness.explanation: If your king has no escape and your back rank is weak, opponent's rook or queen can deliver mate.

discovered_attack.name: Discovered Attack
discovered_attack.trigger: Piece moves to reveal an attack by another piece
discovered_attack.rule: Watch for pieces lined up behind your pieces - moving one might reveal an attack.
discovered_attack.explanation: Discovered attacks are powerful because you make two threats at once.
